parts.title: SSC History: Medieval India — Sultanate & Mughals
parts.intro: Today we study the 'Age of Empires'. Medieval history in SSC is dominated by the 'Delhi Sultanate' and the 'Mughals'. Questions focus on 'Rulers', 'Monuments', and 'Administration'. From the Qutub Minar to the Taj Mahal and the reforms of Akbar—these are the markers of our history. Do you know who started the 'Sijda' system? Or which Mughal king was called 'Zinda Pir'? Let's master the medieval timeline today.

pages.title: Delhi Sultanate (5 Dynasties)
pages.intro: Five Muslim dynasties ruled Delhi from 1206 to 1526, ending with Ibrahim Lodi's defeat at Panipat.

items.label: Slave Dynasty · 1206
items.value: Founded by Qutubuddin Aibak, a former slave soldier

items.label: Khilji Dynasty · 1290
items.value: Alauddin Khilji introduced market reforms and price controls

items.label: Tughlaq Dynasty · 1320
items.value: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's failed token currency of copper/brass coins

items.label: Sayyid Dynasty · 1414
items.value: Brief rule before the Lodi dynasty took over

items.label: Lodi Dynasty · 1451
items.value: Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat in 1526

pages.title: Alauddin Khilji
pages.intro: Sultan of Delhi (1296–1316) known for military reforms and strict market control to stabilize his empire.

items.label: Dagh
items.value: Branding horses with hot iron to prevent swapping in the army

items.label: Chehra
items.value: Written descriptive roll of each soldier's face and appearance

items.label: Market Control
items.value: Government fixed prices of all goods; severe punishment for cheating

pages.title: The Mughal Empire (1526–1857)
pages.intro: Founded by Babur after the First Battle of Panipat, the empire saw its golden age under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan.

branches.label: Babur
branches.value: Founded empire; won First Battle of Panipat, 1526

branches.label: Jahangir
branches.value: Chain of Justice for direct petitions

branches.label: Shah Jahan
branches.value: Golden Age of Architecture; built Taj Mahal

branches.label: Aurangzeb
branches.value: Took title Alamgir; expanded empire to largest size

pages.title: Akbar's Reforms
pages.intro: Mughal emperor Akbar abolished Jizya, introduced the Mansabdari system, and built Fatehpur Sikri with the Ibadat Khana.

rows: Rank-based salary and troop requirements for officials
Capital city with Ibadat Khana for religious debates

pages.title: Monuments
pages.intro: UNESCO World Heritage Sites built by Delhi Sultanate and Mughal rulers, showcasing outstanding historical value.

items.label: Qutub Minar
items.value: Started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, finished by Iltutmish (Slave Dynasty)

items.label: Red Fort
items.value: Built by Shah Jahan in Delhi

items.label: Taj Mahal
items.value: Tomb for Mumtaz Mahal, built by Shah Jahan

items.label: Buland Darwaza
items.value: Gateway at Fatehpur Sikri, built by Akbar to celebrate victory over Gujarat
